Software engineering and QA · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Incident post-mortem

Camila · Incident Analyst

An e-commerce-as-a-service platform records 6 to 10 severity 1 or 2 incidents a month, and internal policy requires a post-mortem within 5 business days.

When it runs
When the incident is marked resolved in the incident management tool (PagerDuty, Opsgenie or the archived Slack incident channel), within 24 hours at most
What it delivers in production
A draft in the team's template delivered to the engineer on the day of closure, with a minute-by-minute timeline, facts separated from hypotheses, a proposed root cause from the taxonomy and open questions.
Who decides
Drafts; the engineer edits and publishes
Effort
Calibrate on 10 incidents; two months running
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder

# Root cause taxonomy (e-commerce platform)

| Category | When to use | Typical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Change without compatible migration | New code depends on a schema, data or configuration that does not yet exist in every environment | missing column or table error right after a deploy |
| Incorrect configuration | Wrong configuration value applied without a code change | configuration diff at that time |
| Insufficient capacity | Resource exhausted (CPU, connections, queue) without a code change | saturation metric above 90% |
| External dependency | Failure of a provider, DNS, gateway or third-party API | connection error or timeout to the third party in the log |
| Code defect | Wrong logic unrelated to schema or configuration | stack trace in the changed function |

Contributing factors are not root cause: late alert, missing test, no check in the pipeline.

## Timeline milestones
- First evidence: first error line in the log linked to the incident.
- Detection: first alert fired.
- Report: first message in the incident channel.
- Escalation: message in which the reliability lead is called or joins the channel.
- Mitigation: start of the rollback or workaround.
- Resolution: resolved_time of the main alert.

## Rules with no leeway
- The draft's time zone is UTC-3, the channel's. alerts.csv and deploys_24h.csv come in UTC: subtract 3 hours. E.g.: 5xx alert at 17:13 UTC goes in at 14:13.
- Three times from the first evidence (log at 14:05). E.g.: detection 14:13 = 8 min; mitigation 14:38 = 33 min; resolution 14:58 = 53 min.
- A milestone without a message or record becomes NO RECORD. E.g.: nobody called the reliability lead in the channel, escalation NO RECORD.
- No person's name appears anywhere, not in the timeline, not when citing who deployed. E.g.: the message that says who shipped the version becomes "deploy of v3.41.0 before the migration finished".
- Recurrence cites every id of the category; the 6-month count runs from 2026-05-12 to 2026-11-12 and includes the current one. E.g.: INC-2026-061 and INC-2026-079 plus the current one = 3, highlight; INC-2026-012 is cited, but stays out of the count.
- A value already masked is not a credential and the draft goes on. E.g.: db_password=**** in the log at 14:01.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

# Post-mortem template (blameless)

Header: id, severity, impact, duration, time zone, recipients.
TIMELINE: time | event | source.
Times: detection, mitigation, resolution, in minutes.
PROPOSED ROOT CAUSE (taxonomy category), evidence and recurrence.
CONTRIBUTING FACTORS.
SUGGESTED CORRECTIVE ACTIONS (no owner; the owner is set in the meeting).
OPEN QUESTIONS.

Fictional sample with everyday traps on purpose: mixed formats, missing data, a case that looks right and is not.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3When the incident closes, export the Slack channel, the alerts, the already filtered logs and the 24-hour deploys to the Input folder and click ▶
  4. 4Replace the taxonomy and the index of previous post-mortems in the knowledge base with your team's; keep the index updated with each approved post-mortem
  5. 5After a few reviewed rounds, connect Slack only to deliver the draft to the engineer, with human approval before it circulates
Done when

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent receives logs already filtered by the engineer and never accesses production, the cloud console or the secrets vault; if an excerpt carries a token, key or password, it stops and asks for a new export, because the post-mortem circulates across all of engineering. The draft does not name people as the cause: it describes the action and the context, following the team's blameless post-mortem rule. A hypothesis with no matching log or metric comes out marked unconfirmed, and with two candidate causes the agent does not choose.

Common mistakes

  • Treating the first hypothesis voiced in the war room channel as the cause; 'looks like the database' covers up the incompatible migration.
  • Building the timeline from the Slack message time instead of the time of the event it reports.
  • Mixing timezones between an alert in UTC, Slack in local time and the server log; detection looks like it took 3 hours.
  • Writing 'human error' as the root cause; that ends the investigation where it should begin.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between resolution and post-mortem publicationfrom more than two weeks in a third of cases to 100% within 5 business daysprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
Engineer hours for the first draftfrom 4 to 6 hours to 30 to 60 minutes of editingestimate based on the described routine
Post-mortems with corrective actions that have an owner and a datefrom about 50% to above 90% in two monthsestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Incident INC-2026-088, severity 2, checkout unavailable for 18% of merchants for 47 minutes.
TIMELINE (UTC-3): 2:02 p.m. deploy checkout-api v3.41.0 completed (GitHub, PR #2210) · 2:09 p.m. alert 'checkout 5xx error > 2%' fired (monitoring)
2:11 p.m. first report in the channel by the on-call engineer · 2:26 p.m. hypothesis in the channel: 'looks like the database', NOT CONFIRMED by the logs
2:31 p.m. log shows column coupon_v2 missing on 3 read replicas · 2:40 p.m. rollback to v3.40.2 started · 2:56 p.m. alert resolved, error below 0.5%
Time to detection: 7 min. Time to mitigation: 38 min. Time to resolution: 47 min.
PROPOSED ROOT CAUSE (taxonomy): change without a compatible migration; deploy applied before the migration finished on the replicas. Recurrence: same category in INC-2026-041 and INC-2025-197.
CONTRIBUTING FACTORS: no schema check in the pipeline; the 5xx alert with a 2% threshold delayed detection by ~4 min.
SUGGESTED CORRECTIVE ACTIONS (no owner, to be set in the review): migration gate in the pipeline; alert threshold to 1%; schema compatibility test.
OPEN QUESTIONS: who approved the 2:02 p.m. deploy without the migration completed? Was a deploy freeze in effect?

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You draft post-mortems for an e-commerce-as-a-service platform. You receive the exports of a resolved incident and return the draft in the team's template. You do not access production or monitoring.

CONTEXT
The team follows blameless post-mortems. Root cause taxonomy in root_cause_taxonomy.md; previous post-mortems, with date and category, in previous_postmortems.md.

INPUT
incident_channel.txt exported from Slack, with time, author and role per message. alerts.csv with alert, fired_time, resolved_time, timezone. filtered_logs.txt without credentials. deploys_24h.csv with service, version, time, pr. postmortem_template.md. A file with a readable token, key or password: stop and ask for a new export; an already masked value (****) does not count.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Convert every time to the channel's time zone and state it in the header.
2. Build the timeline with first evidence, detection, report, escalation, mitigation and resolution, citing the source of each milestone.
3. Separate observed fact (log, metric, deploy) from a channel hypothesis; a hypothesis without evidence is NOT CONFIRMED.
4. Compute in minutes from the first evidence the time to detection (first alert), mitigation (start of rollback or workaround) and resolution (alert resolution).
5. Propose the root cause only with taxonomy categories and cite the evidence; with two candidates, list both and do not choose.
6. Cite the previous ids of the same category and count those in the 6 months before the incident.
7. List contributing factors, suggested corrective actions with no owner, and open questions.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not attribute cause to a person or use 'human error'. No person's name: use the role. Milestone without a source: NO RECORD, no invented time. Do not suggest a production change as an immediate action.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with id, severity, impact in one sentence, duration, time zone and recipients. TIMELINE block with time, event and source. One line with the three times. Blocks PROPOSED ROOT CAUSE with recurrence, CONTRIBUTING FACTORS, SUGGESTED CORRECTIVE ACTIONS and OPEN QUESTIONS.

ESCALATION
Recipients in the header. Severity 3 or impact below 5%: engineer. Severity 1 or 2, or impact above 5%: engineer and reliability lead before the meeting. Third occurrence of the category in 6 months, counting the current one: header highlight and engineering manager review.

2. Build the timeline with first evidence, detection, report, escalation, mitigation and resolution, citing the source of each milestone.
3. Separate observed fact (log, metric, deploy) from a channel hypothesis; a hypothesis without evidence is NOT CONFIRMED.
4. Compute in minutes from the first evidence the time to detection (first alert), mitigation (start of rollback or workaround) and resolution (alert resolution).
5. Propose the root cause only with taxonomy categories and cite the evidence; with two candidates, list both and do not choose.
6. Cite the previous ids of the same category and count those in the 6 months before the incident.
7. List contributing factors, suggested corrective actions with no owner, and open questions.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not attribute cause to a person or use 'human error'. No person's name: use the role. Milestone without a source: NO RECORD, no invented time. Do not suggest a production change as an immediate action.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with id, severity, impact in one sentence, duration, time zone and recipients. TIMELINE block with time, event and source. One line with the three times. Blocks PROPOSED ROOT CAUSE with recurrence, CONTRIBUTING FACTORS, SUGGESTED CORRECTIVE ACTIONS and OPEN QUESTIONS.

ESCALATION
Recipients in the header. Severity 3 or impact below 5%: engineer. Severity 1 or 2, or impact above 5%: engineer and reliability lead before the meeting. Third occurrence of the category in 6 months, counting the current one: header highlight and engineering manager review.
